predecessors.name: Tianwan
predecessors.text: Sichuan and Chongqing, the land of Ming Yuzhen's Longshu and Xia

successors.name: Ming dynasty
successors.text: Sichuan and Chongqing, the land of Ming Yuzhen's Longshu and Xia

rulers.name: Ming Yuzhen
rulers.title: king of Longshu (1360), emperor of the Great Xia (1362)

ledger.x: 1360: Ming Yuzhen takes the title of king of Longshu in Sichuan, refusing Chen Youliang.
1362: Ming Yuzhen becomes emperor of the Great Xia at Chongqing.
May 1371: the Ming army takes northern Sichuan.
August 1371: Chongqing falls and Ming Sheng surrenders.
September 1371: the last Xia defenders surrender.
September 1371: Ming Xia ends with the surrender of Chengdu; Sichuan passes to the Ming.

wars.name: Ming conquest of Sichuan
wars.outcome: Ming victory in 1371: Fu Youde from the north (Mianzhou, May), Tang He and Liao Yongzhong up the Yangtze (Chongqing, August), Chengdu surrenders in September; Ming Sheng is taken to Nanjing and sent to Korea in 1372.

wars.name: Red Turban Rebellions
wars.outcome: Umbrella conflict; Sichuan stays outside Zhu Yuanzhang's state until 1371.

certainty.note: The pages name Sichuan and cities only; the frontier with Yunnan and the Tibetan marches is not described.
